result: P. aeruginosa infection activates the non-canonical inflammasome (caspase-11 and GSDMD cleavage) but specifically inhibits downstream NLRP3 inflammasome activation (caspase-1 activation and IL-1β secretion). This inhibition requires caspase-11 and acts by preventing NEK7-NLRP3 binding, while upstream non-canonical signaling (GSDMD localization, mtDNA release, NUR77-NLRP3 binding) remains intact.

result: VgrG2b from P. aeruginosa is recognized and cleaved by caspase-11/4 at residue D883, generating a free C-terminal fragment. VgrG2b enters macrophages during infection, binds to the caspase-11 p22/p10 complex through its C-terminus, and undergoes enzymatic cleavage both in vitro and in cells.

result: The VgrG2b C-terminal fragment binds specifically to the NACHT-LRR junction of NLRP3 and inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation by competitively blocking NEK7 binding. VgrG2b-C binds NLRP3 with higher affinity than NEK7 (326 vs 681 nM) and does not interact with other inflammasome components (GSDMD, ASC, caspase-1).

result: VgrG2b cleavage by caspase-11 is essential for NLRP3 inhibition during P. aeruginosa infection. Bacteria lacking VgrG2b or carrying the non-cleavable D883A mutation no longer inhibit NLRP3 inflammasome activation, demonstrating that H2-T6SS-mediated VgrG2b delivery and subsequent cleavage are crucial for immune evasion.

result: Mice infected with P. aeruginosa carrying the non-cleavable VgrG2b D883A mutation show significantly improved survival, increased serum and BALF IL-1β levels, decreased bacterial burden, and restored NLRP3 inflammasome activation in lung macrophages, while TNF-α and IL-6 levels remain unchanged.

result: The study identifies a novel immune evasion mechanism where P. aeruginosa hijacks host caspase-11 to cleave its own structural protein VgrG2b, generating an inhibitory fragment. This represents a new paradigm where a bacterial protein requires host protease processing to function as a virulence factor, contrasting with traditional direct immune inhibition mechanisms.
